what_its_for: Flucytosine is an antifungal medicine used to treat serious fungal infections, most commonly infections caused by Candida (a yeast) or Cryptococcus fungi. It is often used together with another antifungal medicine called amphotericin B to treat infections in the blood, urinary tract, or brain (such as fungal meningitis).
how_to_take: Take flucytosine capsules by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the capsules whole with a full glass of water. To help reduce stomach upset and nausea, spread your doses out evenly throughout the day and take them a few at a time over 15 minutes rather than all at once. You can take this medicine with or without food, but taking it with food may help your stomach feel better. Never skip doses and finish the full course of treatment even if you start to feel better.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 50 to 150 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, divided into 4 equal doses taken every 6 hours. Your doctor will decide the exact dose that is right for you based on your weight, kidney function, and the type of infection you have. Do NOT change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular dosing schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store flucytosine capsules at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed. Store in a dry place away from light, heat, and moisture. Do NOT store in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine, as it may increase the risk of side effects. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery if you feel dizzy, confused, or have blurred vision. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen, as this medicine may make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, because flucytosine can interact with many other medications — especially other medicines that affect the kidneys or blood cells.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience any of the following: unusual bruising or bleeding, extreme tiredness or weakness, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, severe nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain, signs of infection such as fever or chills, confusion or mental changes, skin rash or itching, decreased urination or swelling in your feet or ankles, or chest pain. These could be signs of serious side effects affecting your liver, kidneys, or blood cells.
when_it_works: Flucytosine starts working in your body fairly quickly, but it may take several days to weeks before your infection is fully under control and you feel completely better. It is very important to keep taking all of your doses as prescribed, even if you feel better, until your doctor tells you to stop. Stopping too early can allow the infection to come back or become resistant to treatment.
special_populations: Kidney problems: This medicine is removed from your body through the kidneys. If you have kidney disease or poor kidney function, your doctor will need to lower your dose or have you take it less often. Your kidney function and blood levels of the drug will be monitored closely. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Flucytosine may harm an unborn baby, and it is not known if it passes into breast milk. The risks and benefits must be carefully discussed with your doctor. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially those affecting the kidneys and blood cells. Careful monitoring is needed. Children: This medicine can be used in children, but the dose will be carefully calculated by the doctor based on the child's weight.
